headings: Product Innovation, Design, Sustainability and Development
paragraphs: Kontoor Brands, Inc. (collectively with its subsidiaries, "Kontoor," the "Company," "we," "us" or "our") is a global lifestyle apparel company, with a portfolio led by three of the world's most iconic consumer brands: Wrangler®, Lee® and Helly Hansen®. The Company designs, manufactures, procures, sells and licenses apparel, footwear and accessories, primarily under the brand names Wrangler®, Lee® and Helly Hansen®. Our products are sold through wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels in the United States ("U.S.") and internationally, primarily in the Europe, Middle East and Africa ("EMEA"), Asia-Pacific ("APAC") and Non-U.S. Americas regions. We also license the use of our brands in certain regions.

Kontoor is headquartered in the U.S. with a presence in over 90 countries and is focused on leveraging its global platform, strategic sourcing model and supply chain to drive brand growth and deliver long-term value for its stakeholders. Our portfolio of brands has a rich history and heritage of delivering technical and innovative products in the denim, outdoor, workwear, footwear and accessory categories.

We focus on continuously improving the most important elements of our products, which include fit, fabric, finish, technical performance and overall construction, allowing us to engage with more consumers in more places. We leverage innovation and design advancements, as well as the unique heritage and authenticity of our brands to create products that meet our consumers' needs.

The Company operates and reports using a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to December 31 of each year. For presentation purposes herein, all references to years ended December 2025, December 2024 and December 2023 correspond to the 53-week fiscal year ended January 3, 2026, and the 52-week fiscal years ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023, respectively. Accordingly, the year ended December 2025 included an extra week when compared to the year ended December 2024.

On May 31, 2025, we completed the acquisition of a group of companies that own and operate the Helly Hansen® and Musto® brands, collectively referred to as "Helly Hansen," for initial cash consideration of $1.3 billion Canadian dollars, equivalent to $957.5 million U.S. dollars. The purchase price was funded by indebtedness and cash on hand. Helly Hansen® is a premium global outdoor and workwear brand, and Musto® is a premium sailing and outdoor brand. The acquisition of these brands scales Kontoor's penetration in the large and growing outdoor and workwear markets globally, and diversifies Kontoor's portfolio across geographies, categories, consumers and points of distribution. The results of operations of Helly Hansen have been included in the Company's consolidated financial statements since the completion of the acquisition. Refer to Note 2 to the Company's financial statements in this Form 10-K for additional information.

Global macroeconomic conditions that continued to impact the Company during 2025 included inconsistent consumer demand despite recent declines in interest rates, ongoing fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, moderating inflation and global supply chain issues. During 2025 and at the beginning of 2026, the U.S. government enacted and continues to enact significant changes to its tariff regime which increased rates on virtually all imports. The ongoing impact of increased tariff rates and uncertainty regarding the outcomes of trade negotiations is contributing to macroeconomic volatility. In addition, on February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued an opinion regarding certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Powers Act. It is unclear at this time what impact this decision will have on the Company's future financial results, including whether we will be able to obtain refunds of amounts previously collected for such tariffs or the level of replacement tariffs the current U.S. administration may impose through other means.

Inflationary and interest rate pressures have lessened in recent quarters. Despite reduced pressure, these rates have continued to impact us, along with recent increases in product costs and tariffs, as compared to 2024. In 2025, retailers continued to conservatively manage inventory levels as a result of this uncertain macroeconomic environment. The Company has responded to ongoing macroeconomic conditions by controlling expenses, instituting pricing adjustments for our products, investing in our brands and executing our Project Jeanius business transformation.

The increased tariff rates impacted gross margins during 2025 and are expected to continue to impact future periods. The Company continues to evaluate mitigating actions, including the transfer of production within our global supply chain, transformation of our supply chain capabilities, pricing adjustments for our products, supplier partnership initiatives and inventory management. While we anticipate continued uncertainty related to the macroeconomic environment during 2026, including the potential impact of further tariff increases, we believe we are appropriately positioned to successfully manage through operational challenges and cost pressures should they arise. We continue to closely monitor macroeconomic conditions, including consumer behavior and the impact of these factors on consumer demand.

During the third quarter of 2025, the Company closed a portion of its manufacturing facilities. A reduction in our manufacturing facilities and diversification in our sourcing footprint, which is part of our ongoing supply chain transformation, will help to promote flexibility, balance costs, improve speed of service and enhance our sourcing capabilities.

Our principal executive offices are located at 400 N. Elm Street, Greensboro, North Carolina 27401 and our telephone number is 336-332-3400. Our website is www.kontoorbrands.com. Our website and the information contained therein or connected thereto is not incorporated in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
•Iconic Brands With Significant Global Scale

The Wrangler®, Lee® and Helly Hansen® brands are steeped in rich heritage and authenticity, with 79 years, 137 years and 149 years of history, respectively, and have an established global presence in the apparel, outdoor, workwear, footwear and accessories markets across numerous categories and channels of distribution. Products bearing our brands are sold or licensed in more than 90 countries, and we believe they have strong consumer connectivity worldwide with approximately 150 million units sold in 2025. We market our brands and products to highlight their differentiated position and product attributes.

Our Wrangler® and Lee® brands offer lifestyle denim, apparel, footwear and accessories in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, EMEA and APAC through our wholesale and direct-to-consumer businesses and through licensing arrangements. Additionally, we enter into global and regional licensed collaborations to further elevate and support the brands' positioning and recognition. For example, in 2025, our Wrangler® brand, in support of its growing Western and female categories, launched global new collections with GRAMMY Award-winning country music superstar Lainey Wilson, and our Lee® brand partnered with Crayola® on a global apparel collection featuring retired crayon colors.

Our Helly Hansen® brand offers technical performance apparel, workwear, footwear and accessory products in the U.S., Canada, EMEA and through a joint venture arrangement in China. Many of the Helly Hansen® products are designed for winter sports, sailing, lifestyle outdoor activities and workwear engineered for demanding environments. We have partnered with organizations to reinforce the brand's heritage and global recognition including Alpine Canada, New York Yacht Club®, Norwegian Ski Federation, The Ocean Race® and Vail Resorts.

paragraphs: You should carefully consider each of the following risks and all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K in evaluating our business. Our business, prospects, results of operations, cash flows or financial condition could be materially and adversely affected by any of these risks, and, as a result, the trading price of our common stock could decline.
RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY

Global macroeconomic conditions, including inconsistent consumer demand despite recent declines in interest rates, fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates, moderating inflation and global supply chain issues, as well as the ongoing impact of increased tariff rates and uncertainty regarding the outcomes of trade negotiations, continue to adversely impact global economic conditions and have had, and may continue to have, a negative impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

For instance, during 2025 and the beginning of 2026, the U.S. government enacted and continues to enact significant changes to its tariff regime that increased rates on virtually all imports, many of which have gone into effect. This not only contributed to macroeconomic volatility but also adversely impacted our gross margins during 2025 and is expected to continue to impact our gross margins in future periods. In addition, the macroeconomic factors discussed above, primarily tariffs, interest rates and inflation, along with recent increases in product costs, continued to result in retailer actions to conservatively manage inventory levels, which impacted retailers' and the Company's operations in 2025.

We anticipate continued uncertainty related to the macroeconomic environment during 2026, including the potential impact of future tariff increases, and we continue to closely monitor macroeconomic conditions, including consumer behavior and the impact of these factors on consumer demand. Continuing or worsening conditions may have a material adverse impact on our results of operations, cash flows and/or financial condition.

Our revenues and profits depend on the level of consumer spending for apparel, which is sensitive to global economic conditions and other factors. A decline in consumer spending could have a material adverse effect on us.

paragraphs: We are focused on delivering long-term value to our stakeholders, including our consumers, customers, shareholders, suppliers and communities around the world, by accelerating growth, expanding operating margin, increasing capital allocation optionality and establishing the Company as the employer of choice in the industry. Additionally, the integration of Helly Hansen is a strategic focus for the Company, with an emphasis on geographic and category expansion. The Company continues to execute on Project Jeanius, a multi-year comprehensive end-to-end business transformation focused on simplifying processes, optimizing systems and enhancing our global operating model with the goal of creating significant investment capacity through gross and operating margin expansion. In addition, our capital allocation strategy allows us the option to (i) invest in our business, (ii) pay down debt, (iii) provide for a superior dividend payout, (iv) effectively manage our share repurchase authorization and (v) act on strategic acquisition opportunities that may arise.

During 2025, in connection with the Helly Hansen acquisition, the Company incurred acquisition and integration-related costs of $50.8 million comprised of professional and other fees, which are reported in "selling, general and administrative expenses". Acquisition and integration-related costs also included a gain of $24.1 million reported in "other income (expense), net", related to the settlement of foreign currency exchange contracts to hedge the purchase price of the Helly Hansen acquisition. We expect to incur additional costs in future periods as we complete the integration of Helly Hansen.

The Company continued to execute on Project Jeanius during 2025. The Company closed a portion of our manufacturing facilities and incurred restructuring charges of $43.5 million primarily related to severance, employee-related benefits and asset impairments. A reduction in our manufacturing facilities and diversification in our sourcing footprint, which is part of our ongoing supply chain transformation, will help to promote flexibility, balance costs, improve speed of service and enhance our sourcing capabilities. Additionally, the Company incurred transformation charges of $37.1 million related to business optimization activities. During 2024, the Company incurred total restructuring and transformation charges of $38.3 million related to Project Jeanius. We anticipate to incur additional costs associated with Project Jeanius as we continue to execute on this multi-year initiative.
Refer to Note 23 to the Company's financial statements in this Form 10-K for additional information related to restructuring charges.
HIGHLIGHTS OF THE YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 2025

•The acquisition of Helly Hansen was completed on May 31, 2025, and the results of operations have been included in our consolidated financial statements since that date. During the year ended December 2025, the Company incurred $50.8 million of acquisition and integration-related costs which were recorded in "selling, general and administrative expenses".

•During the year ended December 2025, the Company incurred $80.6 million of charges related to the closure of a portion of its manufacturing facilities and business optimization activities, of which $46.3 million were recorded in "cost of goods sold", resulting in an 80 basis point decrease in gross margin for the period, and $34.3 million were recorded in "selling, general and administrative expenses."

•Net revenues of $3.2 billion increased 21% compared to the year ended December 2024, and included a $475.5 million contribution from the Helly Hansen acquisition and an approximate 2% benefit from the 53rd week.

•U.S. Wholesale revenues increased 7% compared to the year ended December 2024, and included a $66.3 million contribution from the Helly Hansen acquisition and an approximate 2% benefit from the 53rd week. U.S. Wholesale revenues represented 64% of total revenues in the current year.

•International Wholesale revenues increased 65% compared to the year ended December 2024, and included a $281.6 million contribution from the Helly Hansen acquisition and a less than 1% benefit from the 53rd week. International Wholesale revenues represented 21% of total revenues in the current year.

•Direct-to-Consumer revenues increased 49% compared to the year ended December 2024, and included a $127.6 million contribution from the Helly Hansen acquisition and an approximate 3% benefit from the 53rd week. Direct-to-Consumer revenues represented 15% of total revenues in the current year.

•Gross margin increased 70 basis points to 45.2% compared to the year ended December 2024, benefiting from product and channel mix, accretion from the Helly Hansen acquisition and benefits from Project Jeanius, partially offset by the net impact of increases in tariff, product costs and pricing adjustments for our products and the $46.3 million of restructuring and transformation charges incurred during the period as discussed in the highlights above.

•Selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenues increased to 34.5% compared to 31.4% for the year ended December 2024, and included $193.7 million of operating expenses attributable to Helly Hansen. Selling, general and administrative expenses in 2025 included $85.1 million of total charges as discussed in the highlights above.

headings: 產品創新、設計、永續性與開發
paragraphs: Kontoor Brands, Inc. (包含其子公司，"Kontoor," "本公司," "我們," "我們"或"我們的") 是一家全球性的生活方式服飾公司，其產品組合由三個世界上最著名的消費者品牌領導：Wrangler®、Lee® 和 Helly Hansen®。本公司設計、製造、採購、銷售及授權服飾、鞋類及配件，主要以 Wrangler®、Lee® 和 Helly Hansen® 品牌名稱為主。我們的產品透過通路及直營通路銷售，銷售範圍包括美國（"U.S.") 及國際市場，主要在歐洲、中東及非洲（"EMEA"）、亞太（"APAC"）及非美國美洲地區。我們也於某些地區授權使用我們的品牌。
Kontoor 設立於美國，並在超過 90 個國家設有據點，專注於運用其全球平台、戰略採購模式及供應鏈，以推動品牌成長並為其利害關係人創造長期價值。本公司品牌組合擁有豐富的歷史與傳統，持續提供技術性與創新性產品於牛仔、戶外、工作服、鞋類及配件等類別。
我們專注於持續改善產品最重要的元素，包括合身度、面料、表面處理、技術性能及整體結構，使我們能與更多消費者在更多地區接觸。我們運用創新與設計進步，以及品牌獨特的歷史與真實性，來創造符合消費者需求的產品。

本公司運作及報告使用 52/53 週會計年度，結算日為每年 12 月 31 日最近的星期六。為呈現目的，本文中所有提及 2025 年 12 月結算、2024 年 12 月結算及 2023 年 12 月結算的參考，對應於 2026 年 1 月 3 日結算的 53 週會計年度，以及 2024 年 12 月 28 日結算的 52 週會計年度，以及 2023 年 12 月 30 日結算的 52 週會計年度。因此，2025 年 12 月結算的年度包含比 2024 年 12 月結算年度多出的一週。

2025 年 5 月 31 日，我們完成了對擁有並經營 Helly Hansen® 和 Musto® 品牌的一組公司的收購， collectively referred to as "Helly Hansen," 初始現金對價為 13 億加拿大元，相當於 9.575 億美國元。購併價格由負債及現金支付。Helly Hansen® 是一個高階全球戶外及工作服品牌，Musto® 是一個高階帆船及戶外品牌。收購這些品牌擴大了 Kontoor 在全球大型且成長中的戶外及工作服市場的佔有率，並使 Kontoor 的產品組合在地理、類別、消費者及銷售通路方面更加多元化。自收購完成後，Helly Hansen 的營運成果已納入本公司合併財務報表。請參閱本 Form 10-K 中本公司財務報表的附註 2 獲取更多資訊。

2025 年持續影響本公司的全球總體經濟條件包括不穩定的消費者需求，儘管近期利率下降，外幣交換率持續波動，通貨膨脹趨緩，以及全球供應鏈問題。2025 年及 2026 年初，美國政府實施並持續實施重大改變其關稅制度的措施，使幾乎所有進口商品的關稅率提高。持續提高的關稅率及對貿易談判結果的不確定性，正在造成總體經濟的波動。此外，2026 年 2 月 20 日，美國最高法院就根據國際緊急權力法所頒布的某些關稅作出意見。目前尚不清楚此決定將如何影響本公司未來的財務結果，包括我們是否能獲得先前收取的這些關稅的退款，或現任美國政府可能透過其他方式施加的替代關稅水平。
通貨膨脹及利率壓力在最近幾個季度已有所緩和。儘管壓力減輕，這些利率仍持續影響我們，加上近期產品成本及關稅的增加，與 2024 年相比。2025 年，零售商因這不確定的總體經濟環境，持續謹慎管理存貨水準。本公司已透過控制費用、對產品進行價格調整、投資品牌及執行 Project Jeanius 商業轉型，來應對持續的總體經濟條件。

提高的關稅率在 2025 年影響了毛利率，並預期會繼續影響未來期間。本公司持續評估緩衝措施，包括在本公司全球供應鏈內轉移生產、轉型供應鏈能力、對產品進行價格調整、供應商合作計劃及存貨管理。儘管我們預期 2026 年仍會有與總體經濟環境相關的持續不確定性，包括進一步關稅增加的潛在影響，我們認為我們已適當準備以成功應對可能出現的運營挑戰及成本壓力。我們持續密切監測總體經濟條件，包括消費者行為及這些因素對消費者需求的影響。
於 2025 年第三季，本公司關閉了部分製造廠區。製造廠區的減少與來源地的多元化，為本公司持續進行的供應鏈轉型的一部分，將有助於提升靈活性、平衡成本、提高服務速度，並強化來源地的採購能力。
本公司主要營業據點位於北卡羅萊納州格林斯堡市楓樹街400號（400 N. Elm Street, Greensboro, North Carolina 27401），電話號碼為336-332-3400。本公司網站為www.kontoorbrands.com。本公司網站及網站內所載資訊或與之相關之資訊，未納入本年度10-K表報表。
•具備顯著全球規模的經典品牌

Wrangler®、Lee® 與 Helly Hansen® 品牌擁有豐富的歷史與真實性，分別有 79 年、137 年與 149 年的歷史，並在服飾、戶外、工作服、鞋類與配件市場，於多種類別與通路中建立全球性存在。標有本公司品牌的產品在超過 90 個國家銷售或授權，本公司相信這些品牌在全球擁有強大的消費者連接，於 2025 年約銷售 1.5 億單位。本公司行銷這些品牌與產品，以強調其差異化定位與產品特性。

本公司 Wrangler® 與 Lee® 品牌透過本公司通路與直營通路業務，以及授權安排，在美國、加拿大、墨西哥、EMEA 與 APAC 提供生活方式牛仔褲、服飾、鞋類與配件。此外，本公司亦進行全球與區域性的授權合作，以進一步提升與支持品牌的定位與認知。例如，在 2025 年，本公司 Wrangler® 品牌為支持其成長中的西部與女性類別，與獲格萊美獎肯定的鄉村音樂巨星 Lainey Wilson 合作推出全球新系列，而本公司 Lee® 品牌則與 Crayola® 合作推出全球服飾系列，特色為 retired 色彩的鉛筆顏色。

本公司 Helly Hansen® 品牌在美國、加拿大、EMEA，以及透過合資安排在中國，提供技術性能服飾、工作服、鞋類與配件產品。許多 Helly Hansen® 產品是為冬季運動、帆船、戶外生活方式活動與工程於嚴苛環境的工作服而設計。本公司已與多個組織合作，以強化品牌的歷史與全球認知，包括 Alpine Canada、New York Yacht Club®、挪威滑雪協會、The Ocean Race® 與 Vail Resorts。

paragraphs: 本公司致力於透過加速成長、擴大營運毛利率、增加資本配置選擇性以及建立本公司為產業首選僱主，以長期創造對股東、消費者、客戶、供應商及全球社區的價值。此外，整合 Helly Hansen 是本公司戰略重點之一，並強調地理與產品類別的擴張。本公司持續執行 Project Jeanius，這是一個多年度的全面性端到端業務轉型計畫，目標在於簡化流程、優化系統並強化全球營運模式，以創造透過毛利率與營運毛利率擴張而產生的顯著投資能力。此外，本公司資本配置策略使本公司有機會 (i) 投資於本公司業務、(ii) 減少債務、(iii) 提供優良的股息發放、(iv) 有效管理本公司股票回購授權、(v) 執行可能出現的戰略收購機會。

2025 年，與收購 Helly Hansen 有關，本公司產生了 5,080 萬美元的收購與整合相關費用，包含專業及其他費用，這些費用計入 "銷售、一般及行政費用"。收購與整合相關費用亦包含 2,410 萬美元的收益，計入 "其他收入（費用），淨額"，與結算外幣交換合約有關，用以對沖 Helly Hansen 收購的購買價格。本公司預期在未來期間會產生額外費用，以完成 Helly Hansen 的整合。

本公司在 2025 年持續執行 Project Jeanius。本公司關閉了部分製造設施，並產生了 4,350 萬美元的重組費用，主要與遣散費、員工相關福利及資產減損有關。減少製造設施與來源地多元化，這是本公司持續進行的供應鏈轉型的一部分，將有助於提高靈活性、平衡成本、提升服務速度並強化來源地能力。此外，本公司產生了 3,710 萬美元的轉型費用，與業務優化活動有關。2024 年，本公司因 Project Jeanius 產生總計 3,830 萬美元的重組與轉型費用。本公司預期會因持續執行此多年度計畫而產生與 Project Jeanius 相關的額外費用。
請參閱本 Form 10-K 財務報表中本公司財務明細的附註 23，以取得與重組費用相關的更多資訊。
2025 年度重點摘要
•Helly Hansen 的收購於 2025 年 5 月 31 日完成，自該日期起，其營運成果已納入本公司合併財務報表。2025 年度，本公司產生了 5,080 萬美元的收購與整合相關費用，計入 "銷售、一般及行政費用"。
•2025 年度，本公司產生了 8,060 萬美元的費用，與關閉部分製造設施及業務優化活動有關，其中 4,630 萬美元計入 "貨品成本"，導致該期間毛利率下降 80 基點，而 3,430 萬美元計入 "銷售、一般及行政費用"。
•營業收入為 3.2 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度成長 21%，包含來自 Helly Hansen 收購的 475.5 百萬美元貢獻，以及約 2% 的 53 週效益。
•美國零售通路營業收入較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度成長 7%，包含來自 Helly Hansen 收購的 66.3 百萬美元貢獻，以及約 2% 的 53 週效益。美國零售通路營業收入在當年佔總營業收入的 64%。
•國際零售通路營業收入較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度成長 65%，包含來自 Helly Hansen 收購的 281.6 百萬美元貢獻，以及少於 1% 的 53 週效益。國際零售通路營業收入在當年佔總營業收入的 21%。
•直營通路營業收入較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度成長 49%，包含來自 Helly Hansen 收購的 127.6 百萬美元貢獻，以及約 3% 的 53 週效益。直營通路營業收入在當年佔總營業收入的 15%。
•毛利率較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度成長 70 基點至 45.2%，受益於產品與通路組合、Helly Hansen 收購的累計效益及 Project Jeanius 的效益，部分抵銷因關稅、產品成本增加及產品價格調整所產生的淨影響，以及當期討論於高亮重點中的 46.3 百萬美元重整與轉型費用。
•銷售及一般與行政費用佔營業收入的百分比增至 34.5%，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度的 31.4%，包含歸屬於 Helly Hansen 的營運費用 193.7 百萬美元。2025 年銷售及一般與行政費用包含討論於高亮重點中的總計 85.1 百萬美元費用。

headings: 總體經濟情勢以及國際政治事件，可能對本公司業務、營運結果、現金流量及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能在整合 Helly Hansen 以及達成收購後預期的成長、成本節省及/或協同效益方面遇到困難。
若本公司無法準確預測產品需求，可能對營運結果造成重大損害。
零售業已面臨財務困難，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
服飾產業競爭激烈，本公司成功取決於能否掌握消費者偏好與產品趨勢，並對不斷變化的市場做出反應。
本公司利潤率可能因邊際壓力增加而下降。
若本公司無法維持品牌形象，可能影響業務及產品的成功。
本公司直接對消費者業務包含可能對營運結果造成重大不利影響的風險。
我們可能無法成功實現我們的商業策略。
我們面臨的風險是，我們的授權經銷商可能無法產生預期的銷售額，或維持我們品牌的價值。
我們的營業收入與現金需求會受到季節性影響。
我們的高階管理人員及其他關鍵員工離職，可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
我們在全球範圍內使用第三方供應商與製造設施，用以取得我們大部分的原材料與成品，這對我們的業務運作構成風險。
如果我們的配送系統遇到問題，我們將產品送到市場的能力可能會受到不利影響。
我們依賴有限數量的北美地區原料來源，我們可能無法及時或足夠地取得合適品質的原材料。
我們可能因非季節性或極端的天氣條件而受到不利影響。
本公司面臨資料安全及隱私權風險，該等風險可能對本公司之營運、營業成果或聲譽造成負面影響。
貿易政策之變更，包括關稅及進出口規範，已對本公司之營業成果、現金流及財務狀況產生負面影響，並可能持續產生負面影響。
本公司之營運及獲利可能受法律、法規、政治及經濟風險之影響。
稅法之變更可能提高本公司之全球稅率，並對本公司之財務狀況及營業成果產生重大影響。
本公司可能產生額外之稅務負擔。
氣候變遷及其相關之立法與法規應對措施，可能對本公司之營運產生負面影響。
本公司可能無法保護、執行或防禦本公司之商標及其他智慧財產權。
未能遵守反貪污、反洗錢及反賄賂法規，可能使本公司遭受處罰及其他負面後果。
工資率波動以及原物料、包括商品成本及成品的價格、可取得性與品質，可能會提高成本。
paragraphs: 您應仔細審慎評估本年度報告表10-K 所載之所有資訊，包括下列風險，以評估本公司之業務。本公司之業務、前景、營運結果、現金流量或財務狀況，可能因任何上述風險而受到重大且不利之影響，因此本公司普通股之交易價格可能下跌。
與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
全球總體經濟情勢，包括儘管近期利率下降，消費者需求仍不穩定、外幣交換率波動、通貨膨脹趨緩以及全球供應鏈問題，以及增加關稅率與貿易談判結果不確定性之持續影響，持續對全球經濟情勢造成負面影響，並已對本公司之業務、營運結果、現金流量與財務狀況造成負面影響，未來可能持續造成負面影響。
例如，在2025年及2026年初，美國政府已實施並持續實施重大關稅制度變更，使幾乎所有進口商品之關稅率提高，其中許多已生效。這不僅導致總體經濟波動，也對本公司2025年毛利率造成不利影響，預期未來期間也會持續對毛利率造成不利影響。此外，上述總體經濟因素，主要是關稅、利率與通貨膨脹，加上近期產品成本增加，導致零售商採取保守方式管理存貨水準，影響零售商及本公司在2025年之營運。
本公司預期在2026年，與總體經濟環境相關之不確定性將持續存在，包括未來關稅增加之潛在影響，本公司持續密切監測總體經濟情勢，包括消費者行為及這些因素對消費者需求之影響。持續或惡化之情況，可能對本公司之營運結果、現金流量及/或財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司之營收與獲利取決於服飾產業之消費者支出水準，而此水準對全球經濟情勢及其他因素較為敏感。消費者支出下降可能對本公司造成重大不利影響。
